cases.answer: You initially wore an Apple Watch Series 8, mainly for step counting and sleep tracking. You added a Garmin HRM-Pro Plus chest strap, purchased from REI for $129.99, and used it on Tuesday and Thursday runs for more accurate heart-rate data. At the end of February, you gave the Apple Watch to your sister and switched around March 5–6 to a 51 mm Garmin Fenix 7X Sapphire Solar, making Garmin your primary tracking platform. You set up solar charging in late March and valued the Garmin’s battery life and always-on transflective display, which remained readable in sunlight without a wrist gesture. You later chose the minimal SolarFace from Connect IQ, showing only time, date, battery, and steps, after rejecting a six-complication face as too cluttered. You turned off almost all phone notifications because you wanted the watch for time and body tracking without screen interruptions. When the Fenix developed a minor sensor issue, the warranty team chose to repair your original watch rather than replace it, preserving the sapphire lens and solar charging you valued. Your latest stated setup remained the repaired Fenix 7X Sapphire Solar with the HRM-Pro Plus chest strap, with no planned switch to other gear.
